correctness.rationale: Clipping is the Frobenius projector by the singular-value trace inequality and scalar minimization. At X=(1+s)uv^T, symmetric dilation gives a simple positive eigenvalue with a uniform gap as s decreases to zero, so the derivative of the leading singular outer product remains bounded. Differentiating X-(sigma_1-1)uv^T gives the asserted tangent limit in coordinate operator norm. The selected row sum is 1+|u_i v_j| ||u||_1 ||v||_1-2u_i^2 v_j^2. With fixed absolute selected entries x,y, equal absolute tails attain both Cauchy inequalities, including the endpoints. The explicit half-mass coordinates give the lower bound. Independently, for input difference h and output difference g, firm nonexpansivity gives ||g-h/2||_2 <= ||h||_2/2, hence the upper bound globally without assumptions on differentiability. The bounds coincide at 2 by 2. The only jointly leading term in the rank-one formula is bounded by sqrt((m-1)(n-1))/4 and attained to leading order by x=y=1/sqrt(2); the single-root terms vanish upon division by sqrt(mn) if both dimensions diverge. No finite-pair equality or unrestricted leading constant is established in general dimensions.
residual_risks: No formal certificate, external attestation, or general exact value of L_{m,n} is claimed.

value.rationale: The entrywise modulus is a natural worst-case stability benchmark for a standard matrix projection, different from its Euclidean modulus. The independent left/right tangent optimization gives a sharp and usable rectangular benchmark, with a mechanism showing order growth even though the operation is Frobenius nonexpansive. The universal upper bound or a repeated 2 by 2 number alone would not justify this assessment.
residual_risks: The theorem does not cover perturbations restricted by convolutional structure or any all-dimension global sharp coefficient.
